top_story: A Gaza City building already damaged by Israeli strikes collapsed on 16 September, killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, and trapping scores more from roughly 100 displaced families as rescuers worked without sufficient heavy machinery. The sequence matters: prior bombardment created the structural failure, and the delayed collapse turned chronic displacement and degraded civil defense capacity into a mass-casualty event for civilians already living in precarious shelter. In Iran, fresh evidence of the state’s coordinated killings, torture, and sexual abuse during the 2022 protest crackdown sharpens the picture of a repression system that has carried into even deadlier violence this year. Taken together, the day’s developments show governments and militaries across the region converting earlier coercive force into later civilian harm, deepening public vulnerability long after the initial attack or arrest.
